blocks.text: Langley City homes listed and sold, June to October 2026

Langley City, October 2026. Detached houses: 67 listed at month end and 5 sold in October, a sales ratio of 7% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 185 listed at month end and 36 sold in October, a sales ratio of 19% (a balanced market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 42 sold over 5 months against an average of 69.2 listed, about 8.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 12 sold. Condos and townhomes: 142 sold over 5 months against an average of 192.2 listed, about 6.8 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was October with 36 sold.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: The City of Langley is a separate municipality from the Township of Langley, with its own council, Official Community Plan (OCP) and zoning bylaw; this page covers City homes only.
The page itself describes the City as centred on a compact downtown, and Fraser Highway is the corridor its attached stock clusters on.
Plan, zoning-map and development-plan detail for the City is held in full in one place — see the langleycity note.
The future Langley City Centre SkyTrain station is planned at 203 Street, at the downtown end of the Surrey Langley SkyTrain extension.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: the housing stock

items.t: The City's shelf is attached-led: Fraser Highway condos and townhomes carry most of the City's listings, with detached ranchers on the residential streets behind the corridor.
A 55-plus unit appears in the City's own feed character at 20600 53a Avenue, so age-restricted strata product exists inside the City as well as market condos.
The Unity Building at 20769 Fraser Highway is the named condo building visible on the page's first screen of listings.
Detached examples on the page sit on 203 Street and 204 Street, the north–south residential grid west of downtown.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Housing rules here are the City's own: small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH), suite, garden suite and carriage home rules are stated in full in the langleycity note, which carries the City's plan and zoning detail.

The one rule a homes buyer meets first: a suite shown in a listing must be permitted, inspected and in the City's secondary suites registry, with the registered owner living on the lot — full text in the langleycity note.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: City Hall is at 20399 Douglas Crescent, and the City charges a 2.2 percent processing fee on credit-card property tax payments.
The City's vision page promises SkyTrain by the end of 2029 while the project page says late 2029 — the same target in two wordings; use the project page for status.
Langley City Centre station will include one of the extension's three transit exchanges, so bus routes will re-orient to 203 Street when the line opens — check current.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: development and new projects

items.t: Surrey Langley SkyTrain, Langley City Centre station at 203 Street: STATUS — under construction, anticipated in-service late 2029; read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: costs and taxes

items.t: City-wide cost facts are stated in full in one place — see the langleycity note for the City's 2026 total residential tax rate per $1,000, the water flat fee and consumption charge, and the July 2 due date.
The City-specific payment fact for a new owner: paying property taxes by credit card carries a 2.2 percent processing fee.
No SkyTrain station operates in the City today; the extension now under construction ends at 203 Street in Langley City Centre with an anticipated in-service date of late 2029.
The extension adds eight stations over 16 kilometres from King George Station, primarily on an elevated guideway along Fraser Highway.

blocks.text: Langley City Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: For a home with a suite, ask for the City registry record and the building permit, not the listing text — the registry requirement is stated in the langleycity note.
For a lot near the future station, check the Transit-Oriented Area land-use update that came with the 2025–2026 bylaw package before assuming current density is final — check current.

faq.q: Which schools are physically inside the City?
faq.a: Six School District No. 35 (Langley) schools sit inside the City: Douglas Park Community at 5409 206 Street, Nicomekl Elementary at 20050 53 Avenue, Blacklock Fine Arts Elementary at 5100 206 Street, Uplands Elementary at 4471 207a Street, H D Stafford Middle at 20441 Grade Crescent, and Langley Secondary at 21405 56 Avenue. Catchments are address-based, so confirm the exact address with the district.

faq.q: Is the hospital inside the City?
faq.a: No. Langley Memorial Hospital at 22051 Fraser Highway is the hospital for both Langleys, and Fraser Health lists its address in the Township of Langley, immediately outside the City boundary. It provides 24/7 emergency, general and internal medicine, general surgery and maternity services, so City buyers use it daily without it being a City building.

faq.q: When does SkyTrain actually reach the City?
faq.a: The Surrey Langley SkyTrain project extends the Expo Line 16 kilometres from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with eight stations and a transit exchange at Langley City Centre. The project's current anticipated in-service date is late 2029. Until then the City is bus-served, so price a home on today's transit, not the station rendering.

faq.q: Are City taxes the same as Township taxes?
faq.a: No, the two municipalities set separate rates and send separate notices. The City's 2026 total residential rate and utility structure are stated in full in the langleycity note. A Township rate applied to a City home, or the reverse, gives the wrong carrying cost, so check the municipality on the tax notice itself.

faq.q: What are Langley City's secondary suite rules?
faq.a: Under Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300, a suite must not exceed the lesser of 100 m² and 40% of the building's gross floor area, the registered owner must reside on the lot, at least one extra off-street parking space is required, and the suite must be permitted, inspected and recorded in the City's secondary suites registry (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, read 2026-11-01).
